title: Social and professional contexts of legal commitment
shortTitle: Social and professional contexts of legal commitment
summary: The setting of an undertaking affects whether the parties’ words reasonably carry legal obligations.
notes: Cohen’s earlier opinion treats the source-reporter promise as ethically serious but unsuitable for an ordinary contract theory; the later opinion allows estoppel. Social arrangements, rides, family commitments, and medical reassurance raise related contextual issues. The Balfour supplement is missing, so the casebook’s references support only its placement here. The text also distinguishes unmarried parties’ capacity to contract from assumptions drawn from marriage or family relations.

sources.label: Farnsworth et al., Contracts: Cases and Materials, 10th ed. (2023), pp. 183–187. Open assigned page 183.
